subject: CSA: Exportable control snippets and runtime evidence retrieval plan
messages:
From: Nadia Patel <nadia@orion-health.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@orion-health.com
Date: 2028-07-21T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: CSA control text + runtime log samples for evidence package

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. As part of our procurement diligence and upcoming internal CSA review, our security team needs two deliverables so we can finish the control narrative and provide a copy to auditors:

1) Exportable control text snippets mapped to the relevant CSA control IDs (CSV or docx is fine). We want short, self-contained sentences that we can paste into our questionnaire and label with the control ID (e.g. CCM-EDM-01).
2) Runtime evidence samples showing how requests are handled in production (log excerpts or URLs to short log bundles). Specifically we need:
   - an access log sample showing request timestamp, model variant, request id, and requester IP (redacted as needed)
   - a KV/cache miss/hit example for a cached prefix scenario

Can you confirm if you can provide both by end of week? Also please advise the best artifact names and any short instructions auditors need to interpret the samples.

If there are any constraints (PII, retention policy, or HSM-backed keys) that affect what you can share, call that out. We can accept redacted samples.

Appreciate it,

—Nadia
Nadia Patel
Senior Product Security Manager, Orion Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Nadia Patel <nadia@orion-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-21T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: CSA control text + runtime log samples for evidence package

Hi Nadia —

We can provide both. High-level plan and what to expect:

- Exportable control snippets: we will produce a single doc (csa-exportable-snippets-v1.docx) with 1–2 sentence controls mapped to CSA IDs, the assertion text, and a short pointer to the underlying artifact (drive link + file name). This will be suitable to paste into questionnaires.
- Runtime log samples: we will provide short log bundles (3 small excerpts) and a text file with signed URLs (runtime-log-sample-urls.txt) that contain redacted request_id, timestamp, model, and outcome. The logs will be scrubbed of PII and real IPs will be masked.

Constraints / notes:
- We will not include raw customer prompts in samples. If a specific prompt example is required for traceability, we can provide a redacted synthetic example with the same token length distribution.
- HSM and key rotation details will be represented in the control snippet and by referencing the authorization artifacts; we will not share private keys.

Proposed timeline: initial artifacts to you by EOD Friday (2028-07-21 23:59 PDT). If that works, Marissa will coordinate the packaging and Ben will produce the log extracts. Jonas will review the control text and mark any items that need product-owner attestation.

Confirm and I’ll kick off the internal checklist.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Attachments: csa-exportable-snippets-v1.docx (draft) — will replace with final; runtime-log-sample-urls.txt (placeholder)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: action items for Orion Health CSA artifacts (owner assignments)

Team —

Following Nadia’s ask (thread above), here’s the exact split and minimal acceptance criteria so we can deliver by EOD:

Marissa — package owner/QA
- Review csa-exportable-snippets-v1.docx for clarity and auditor-readiness. Ensure each control snippet has: control ID, 1-line snippet, reference to artifact, and a single-sentence validation note.
- Add a short readme block at top of doc that explains redaction approach.

Jonas — product attestation reviewer
- Review 10 prioritized controls (I’ll flag CCM identities) for correctness and add attestation phrases where needed ("Product owner attests that...").

Ben — log extraction
- Run extraction-script.py on prod logging for the last 30 days to surface 3 representative traces:
   A) normal request path (cache miss -> model infer)
   B) cached prefix (cache hit)
   C) fallback (primary variant unavailable -> fallback activated)
- Output should be zipped and uploaded to a signed URL list (runtime-log-sample-urls.txt). Mask requester IPs, redact user prompts, keep request_id and timing fidelity.

Operational notes:
- Attach extraction-script.py to the deliverables; include a one-paragraph explanation of the extraction query and retention-safe redaction.
- If we find traces containing customer PII, stop and escalate; we will not include them.

Let’s aim to have a review sync at 2:30pm PDT if needed (15 min). I’ll assemble the package and send to Nadia once you sign off.

Thanks — Kim

Nadia —

Attached are the deliverables we discussed. Summary below and quick interpretation guide for your auditors.

Deliverables attached:
- csa-exportable-snippets-v1.docx — 78 concise control snippets mapped to CSA IDs. At the top: readme with redaction policy and how to map snippets to our evidence artifacts.
- runtime-log-sample-urls.txt — 3 signed URLs (48h expiry) that point to zipped log excerpts. Each file includes a README that explains fields: request_id (uuid), ts_utc, model_variant, action, cache_status, outcome.
- extraction-script.py — script used to pull the excerpts; we included the exact query and a note about the scrubber that replaced IPs with masked values (x.x.x.x).

Auditor quick notes:
- All logs are redacted to remove prompt content and IP addresses; timing relationships and request IDs are preserved so you can confirm sequence and behavior (cache hit/miss, fallback).
- HSM and key rotation controls are documented in snippet CCM-CRY-02 with a pointer to our key management attestation (see snippet line 34 + Drive link).

If Veridian wants an additional walkthrough of the zipped logs, we can schedule 30 minutes next week. Otherwise, please confirm receipt and whether the artifacts satisfy your immediate needs.

Thanks — Kim

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
